explanations: Aliquot stringing gave grand instruments a more powerful sound, a longer sustain and a richer tone.
In the 19th century a cast iron frame was adopted, which allowed much greater string tensions.
Most notes have three strings, except in the bass, which graduates from one to two.
Pedals at the base lift the dampers off the strings, so notes go on sounding after the keys are released.
Modern instruments have 88 black and white keys, and pressing one swings a felt-coated wooden hammer at the strings.

sources.excerpt: Aliquot stringing gave grand pianos a more powerful sound, a longer sustain, and a richer tone.
In the 19th century, influenced by Romantic music trends, the fortepiano underwent changes such as the use of a cast iron frame, which allowed much greater string tensions.
Most notes have three strings, except for the bass, which graduates from one to two.
Notes can be sustained when the keys are released by the use of pedals at the base of the instrument, which lift the dampers off the strings.
Modern pianos have a row of 88 black and white keys—with the exception of the Bosendörfer and Stuart & Sons pianos—and tuned to a chromatic scale in equal temperament.
When a key is depressed, the strings inside are struck by felt-coated wooden hammers.
